clue.text: Outwardly merry, I have to enjoy myself

definitions.note: the clue speaks in the first person; the answer is the general verb phrase

indicators.note: outwardly says the phrase for merry stands outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: lit up is slang for tipsy, i.e. merry with drink
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A cheerful speaker announces that they are going to have a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' puts LIT UP around IVE: L + IVE + IT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a lively, extravagant good time is the idiom's meaning, so it fits enjoying oneself.

clue.text: Vessel not so dark

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships

explanation.definitionFit: A barge used to ferry cargo is one sense, and paler in shade is the comparative sense.

clue.text: Left a cove making a U-turn

indicators.note: making signals the letters are reformed to make the answer

explanation.surface: Turning left at a bay means doubling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy, French for turned face.

clue.text: Is love dead? Divorce is the answer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
the late means the dead

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about lost romance, answered by separation.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce here is the verb to separate or cut off, a synonym.

clue.text: Out of bed, cleaned in a beehive

definitions.note: the phrase is adjectival, describing hair worn that way

parts.note: up means risen, out of bed
swept means cleaned with a brush

explanation.surface: Someone gets up and tidies a hive of bees.
explanation.walkthrough: A beehive is a tall 1960s hairstyle, not a home for bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair brushed upward and piled high describes a beehive hairdo.

clue.text: Many at start of the market shop around

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the word market
around turns the word for the shop back to front

parts.note: a dairy is a shop selling milk and its products

explanation.surface: Lots of people turn up early at the market stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns DAIRY into YRIAD, which follows M from 'market'.
explanation.definitionFit: Countless or a vast number, a synonym for many.

clue.text: In the story, I am involved with Zen more than once

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are jumbled
more than once tells us to take the word Zen twice

explanation.surface: In a tale, the narrator gets caught up in Buddhist practice repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' doubles ZEN; 'involved' jumbles IAM with ZENZEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey (story in US spelling) is a floor; this one is a low intermediate floor.

clue.text: In colour that's in reverse

indicators.note: In placed before the colour means the following pieces go in it

parts.note: red is a colour
sc, short for Latin scilicet, means that is to say

explanation.surface: Something coloured is shown backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is a dictionary abbreviation for 'scilicet', i.e. 'namely, that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse a decision is to revoke or cancel it.

clue.text: Men wandering in the Far East forgetting everything

definitions.note: the phrase describes the condition the noun names

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the region

parts.note: Asia is the eastern continent

indicators.note: wandering means the men's letters stray out of order

explanation.surface: Lost men roam the Orient with no memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' makes MNE, which 'in' places within ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Total memory loss is the medical term's meaning.

clue.text: Sea god cold in the mist that's about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole built string is read backwards

parts.note: Zeus is the chief Greek god

indicators.note: in places the illness inside the word for mist

parts.note: fog is thick mist
a cold or flu, a common infection

explanation.surface: A deity of the sea, chilled, wanders in a swirling mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts FLU inside FOG to give FOFLUG; with ZEUS before it, 'that's about' reverses ZEUSFOFLUG.
explanation.definitionFit: This gulf is an arm of the Red Sea at the northern end, by Egypt's canal.

clue.text: Transmitted in 16

definitions.meaning: ... as a message or signal is dispatched
16 is ecstasy; old slang for enraptured, in ecstasy

explanation.definitionFit: A message dispatched has been sent, and old jazz slang uses the word for someone carried away in rapture.

clue.text: Best with a beer — a novel

definitions.text: Best with a beer — a novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recommendation to read a good book with a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges BESTWITHABEERA. The whole clue defines: it is Charles Kingsley's 1863 children's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley's Victorian fantasy about a chimney sweep turned river creature is a famous book.

clue.text: Stand-in swallows a testing substance

indicators.note: swallows means the word for stand-in takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a regent rules in place of a monarch, a stand-in

explanation.surface: An understudy gulps down something being tested in the lab.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry it is a compound used to detect or produce a reaction, so a testing substance.

clue.text: Deny holding it up following a round that's clear

indicators.note: holding means the word for deny contains the next pieces

parts.note: to negate is to deny

indicators.note: following places the turned word after the round letter

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: Refusing to hold anything up after a round of drinks is clear-cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI, placed after O; 'holding' puts OTI inside NEGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To get past an obstacle successfully, as a horse clearing a fence.

clue.text: Knock the breath out of woman, one given to talking

parts.note: to wind someone is to knock the breath out of them
bag is derogatory slang for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone punches a chatty woman in the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome, long-winded talker; idiomatic for a chatterbox.

clue.text: 37 degrees of kindred — only part of the whole race

parts.note: blood means family relationship, kindred

parts.words: only part of the whole race
parts.note: a heat is one preliminary round of a race

explanation.surface: Relatives get a degree of warmth from a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal human body temperature is about 37 Celsius.

clue.text: Interview a servant something's leaked out

definitions.note: the phrase reads as a clause; the answer names what has leaked

parts.note: to see someone can mean to interview them, as an employer sees applicants
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A footman is questioned after secrets get out.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that has slowly oozed through a gap; a noun for leakage.

clue.text: Not worried about the Conservative way to attain bliss

indicators.note: about means the relaxed word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: easy means relaxed, not worried
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Unconcerned about the Tories, one finds a path to happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelming joy or rapture, a synonym of bliss.

clue.text: Staff originally couldn't abide the stink from it

definitions.text: Staff originally couldn't abide the stink from it

parts.note: a pole is a staff

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Staff members could not stand the smell coming from an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the beast: a small mammal famous for a foul smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A European weasel-like mammal noted for its strong odour.

clue.text: Boredom at work? Retire here

indicators.note: at work means the letters are busy being reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Fed up with being bored in the office, someone wants to quit and stay home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' means go to bed, not leave employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night means going to bed, done in a sleeping room.

clue.text: It provides drink for sheep trapped between railway lines

indicators.note: trapped between means the animal sits inside two other pieces

parts.note: BR (British Rail) and Ry are both abbreviations for railway
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A water supply for a sheep stranded on the tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway; Ry is a standard abbreviation for railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery is where beer is made, so it supplies alcoholic refreshment.

clue.text: Compere is in love, in part

indicators.note: the first in means the little word goes inside the compere

parts.note: a DJ (disc jockey) compères a show
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A host has fallen partly in love.
explanation.definitionFit: To part as a verb is to separate, to detach one thing from another.

clue.text: Camion's out of order

indicators.note: out means the letters are out of place and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken-down lorry: the truck is not working.
explanation.walkthrough: A camion is a lorry. The definition is 'of order', i.e. of the Freemasons' order.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Freemasons, a fraternal brotherhood.

clue.text: 19-1 — second team's creased

parts.note: 19 down is disjoin, meaning split
the number 1 is one
a team is a side; with the 's, sides

explanation.surface: A cross-reference sum, then a second team is crumpled.
explanation.walkthrough: The '19-1' looks like a score or a sum; it reads as 'disjoin' then 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be creased up is British slang for laughing helplessly, like splitting with laughter.

clue.text: A sound spot of brandy

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the word for spot is pronounced

parts.note: a mark is a spot or stain

explanation.surface: Asking for a decent drop of brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit distilled from grape pressings, a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Girl meeting lad bearing the French name — she lost her head

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

indicators.note: bearing means the word for lad carries the French article inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A girl dates a boy with a French name, then is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII's second wife was beheaded in 1536.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's second queen was executed by beheading at the Tower of London.

clue.text: Recurrent crack in elm tree

indicators.note: recurrent, read as running back, turns the whole built string backwards
in puts the attempt inside the tree's name

parts.note: to have a crack is to have a try

explanation.surface: A split keeps reappearing in the bark of an elm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TRY inside ELM to make ELTRYM; 'Recurrent' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen shrub or small tree with fragrant white flowers, sacred to Venus.

clue.text: Fruit you can hear (and almost, see) is soporific

indicators.note: you can hear tells us to take the fruit's word by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the word for see

parts.note: to notice is to see

explanation.surface: Some fruit makes noises and nearly appears, which sends you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: HIP said aloud gives HYP; 'almost' clips NOTICE to NOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something inducing sleep, near-synonyms.
